description: The jabberwock's N-DIMENSIONAL representation (docs/jabberwock_representation_design.md): the grid is a RENDER, obs = pi(phi); (cy,cx) are just two coordinates of a longer state vector phi. This builds phi as a Vec on each Region (a superset of position: cy, cx, drow, dcol, rvalue, count) and runs the SAME predict->surprise->fold loop over phi instead of 2D — 'the loop I already run, in the thing itself instead of its shadow.' The grid is recovered as pi(phi) = Nth(phi,0..1); a basis change is Rotate(phi)=Dot-over-axes (no new primitive — the agent's Dot). Core skill: represent interaction/dynamics projection-independently; the game is the means, the representation skill is the end.

microtheory.name: nd_representation
microtheory.description: phi = the N-D state; the grid is pi(phi), one projection; predict the next phi, fold; rotate (Dot-over-axes) to the natural frame.

rules.name: build_phi
rules.comment: Lift each Region's observation into its N-D descriptor phi = Vec(cy, cx, drow, dcol, rvalue, count). (cy,cx) are two of its coordinates; the grid is one projection pi(phi)=Nth(phi,0..1). phi is a Tuple-valued attr.

rules.name: predict_phi
rules.comment: The forward model IN N-D: predict the next phi = constant velocity in the state (position advances by its velocity; velocity/identity persist). Written as next_phi_pred (a Vec) + clocked=1, so the engine's clock-edge fold commits next_phi_pred->phi_pred — the SAME predict->fold mechanism as Stage 0, now over the N-D state. surprise = ||phi_obs - phi_pred|| (the N-D residual; measured against the prediction committed last tick).
